title: Collect and Extract Biomass from Cyanobacteria
author: Ricardo M. Borges

steps.title: Grow cyanobacterial cultures
steps.instruction: Allow each Erlenmeyer flask culture to grow until a substantial biomass is formed (visual estimate of ~80‑90% extraction after 28 days) with an empirical limit of four months per specimen; interrupt growth earlier if excess biomass, cell death, or other issues arise.

steps.title: Transfer culture and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Transfer the culture medium from each flask to a labeled 50 mL Falcon‑type conical centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 3011 × g (4500 rpm) at 4 °C for 15 min, discard the supernatant, and repeat transfer and centrifugation until all aqueous content is removed. Record the volume of biomass obtained (photo for file).

steps.title: Filter and dry biomass (if possible)
steps.instruction: If feasible, filter the harvested biomass and dry it; otherwise proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Lyophilize dried biomass
steps.instruction: Place each properly identified biomass sample in a clean, semi‑screwed Falcon tube, lyophilize until completely dry, record observations in the metadata, and store the dried samples at –20 °C.

steps.title: Verify labels and organize tubes
steps.instruction: Check that label codes match the list of dried biomass samples. Prepare new 2 mL screw‑cap microtubes for dried biomass and new 2 mL Eppendorf‑type microtubes for extracts; label all tubes according to the sample table and use only brand‑new consumables.

steps.title: Weigh biomass into microtubes
steps.instruction: Weigh 50 mg of dried biomass and transfer it to a 2 mL screw‑cap microtube. Include extraction blanks: empty vials placed at the beginning, at the end of the sample sequence, and after every ten samples.

steps.title: Add polar extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL of methanol‑water (1:1, v/v) to each screw‑cap microtube containing the biomass.

steps.title: Homogenize and sonicate (polar)
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube for 20 seconds, then place the tubes in an ultrasonic bath for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge polar extracts
steps.instruction: Centrifuge all tubes at 24 900 × g (16 000 rpm) for 15 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect first polar supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer 750 µL of the supernatant from each tube into a new, properly labeled 2 mL Eppendorf‑type microtube.

steps.title: Second polar extraction
steps.instruction: Add an additional 750 µL of methanol‑water (1:1, v/v) to each tube, vortex 20 seconds, ultrasonic bath 5 minutes, centrifuge at 24 900 × g (16 000 rpm) for 15 minutes at 4 °C, and collect 750 µL of supernatant into a new labeled 2 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Prepare QC‑pool sample
steps.instruction: Aliquot 50 µL from each individual extract, pool the aliquots in a 20 mL flask, then divide the pooled QC sample into four new labeled analytical vials; store any remaining volume for future analyses (e.g., 2D NMR).

steps.title: Add zirconia beads
steps.instruction: Add approximately 200 µL of 1 mm zirconia beads to each 2 mL screw‑cap microtube containing biomass (treat blanks identically).

steps.title: Add non‑polar extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL of dichloromethane‑methanol (2:1, v/v) to all screw‑cap microtubes.

steps.title: FastPrep homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize each tube for 60 seconds at the highest speed (6 m/s) using the FastPrep‑24 homogenizer.

steps.title: Centrifuge non‑polar extracts
steps.instruction: Centrifuge all tubes at 24 900 × g (16 000 rpm) for 15 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect first non‑polar supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer 750 µL of supernatant from each tube into a new, properly labeled 2 mL Eppendorf‑type microtube.

steps.title: Second non‑polar extraction
steps.instruction: Add another 750 µL of dichloromethane‑methanol (2:1, v/v) to each tube, vortex for 20 seconds, ultrasonic bath for 5 minutes, centrifuge at 24 900 × g (16 000 rpm) for 15 minutes at 4 °C, and collect 750 µL of supernatant into the same 2 mL Eppendorf tubes used previously.

steps.title: Duplicate non‑polar collection
steps.instruction: Collect an additional 750 µL of supernatant from each tube into the same 2 mL Eppendorf‑type microtubes (as previously done).

steps.title: Evaporate extracts (first)
steps.instruction: Place all collected extracts in a SpeedVac and evaporate until completely dry; store the dried residues at –80 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Evaporate extracts (second)
steps.instruction: Repeat SpeedVac evaporation of any remaining extracts until dry and store at –80 °C until prepared for analysis.
